transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Aisha, Tom, Priya, Samir (Riverstone)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20271110-riv-8372 (note: link placeholder)

Auto-generated Summary:
Maya: Quick orientation, show Console's per-route views and how to map routes to product features, then deep dive on cost breakdown. Leo: demos of telemetry filters, commit maps, and the Optimize suggestions engine. Customer asks about VPC, KMS, data residency and pilot sizing. End with clear next steps to send pricing and run benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll plan for about 45 minutes, quick intro then Leo will jump into the Console and we'll leave time for Q&A, sound good?
[00:12] Aisha (Riverstone): Yep that's great, thanks Maya, excited to see the per-route stuff — we currently have, like, multiple endpoints and it's a pain to map cost back to product teams.
[00:22] Maya: Totally, that's what we're aiming for. Quick intros? I'll let you go around.
[00:25] Aisha: Aisha, Head of ML, I own models and deployments.
[00:28] Tom: Tom Keller, Platform Eng, I manage our infra and networking.
[00:31] Priya: Priya, FinOps, I look at cost allocation and chargeback.
[00:34] Samir: Samir, Security.
[00:36] Leo (Redwood SE): Leo, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll demo telemetry and the Optimize recommendations.
[00:41] Maya: Great, quick context on Riverstone — you mentioned you're running OpenAI today plus some in-house inference?
[00:47] Aisha: Yeah openai for most text gen, some embeddings in-house, and we're experimenting with a smaller hosted thing for sensitive data — its kinda split so attribution is messy.
[00:58] Maya: Understood. Two things we'll show: per-route dashboards that let you tag routes to products and teams, and cost breakdowns so you can slice by model, quantization, and region. Then Leo will show Optimize suggestions — e.g., batching configs and KV cache usage estimates.
[01:15] Tom: One quick thing, we need to know about VPC/private options, we can't send certain data off-net; encryption at rest, KMS, yeah.
[01:23] Maya: Yep we'll cover that — Private deployments, V P C options, and KMS/HSM integration. Also our hosted product can be configured with strict retention rules if that's helpful.
[01:33] Leo: Jumping into the Console — sharing my screen now, tell me if you see the dashboard.
[01:38] [screen share noise] 
[01:42] Leo: So this is the main telemetry view, at the top is total token usage over time, then below is per-route cards. Each route can be tagged with product, team, environment. You can also attach a SLA tag and a routing policy; for example route A is low-latency, route B is cost-saver.
[02:05] Priya: How do you map mapping works — is it manual tags or auto-ingest?
[02:10] Leo: Good q. We support both — SDK/headers for auto tags, and a UI tag mapping for older apps. Many customers start with header-based mapping so it's automatic. There is also a rules engine to rewrite route names if your infra uses ephemeral ids.
[02:28] Aisha: Nice. Can we split cost between prompt tokens and completion tokens? Our product has long prompts.
[02:33] Leo: Yep that's the token-level breakdown — you'll see prompt vs completion, model compute cost, and then a column for any caching saved tokens. Also we estimate cost if you apply a quantization profile or switch to a cheaper model variant.
[02:48] Tom: The estimate accuracy — how close is it to real billing?
[02:52] Leo: We derive unit economics from runtime telemetry — measured throughput, per-token GPU time, and your cost profile if you're on Dedicated; for hosted customers we provide a measured baseline. It's an estimate but in our experience within 5-12% for steady workloads, but bursty patterns can vary.
[03:09] Priya: Sweet, that variance is fine. Can you show route-level alerts — like sudden spike in cost for route X?
[03:16] Leo: Yep, alerts panel — you can set thresholds by tokens, cost, or latency p95. Here's an example where we alerted that route "claims-extract" spiked due to a model change.
[03:30] [laughter] Aisha: That's exactly our problem last month.
[03:32] Maya: We'll also show how to roll back model variants automatically with fallback policies; that helps when a new model causes token blowups.
[03:42] Leo: Now Optimize suggestions — we run an analysis of request distributions, sequence length histogram, and KV cache hit rates. From that we recommend batching windows, prefix caching, and quantization profiles.
[03:58] Tom: Does Optimize actually run in prod or just a simulator?
[04:02] Leo: It generates exact config suggestions and a simulated cost savings based on your historical traces. If you approve, we can push configs to Dedicated pools or provide a deployment yaml for Private. For hosted we can apply changes as part of a canary.
[04:17] Priya: Can you demo a concrete before/after?
[04:20] Leo: Sure. Here's a route where enabling prefix KV cache and a 50ms batching window reduced tokens and lowered per-request GPU time by 28% — simulated savings showed a 22% cost reduction for that route.
[04:38] Aisha: How does cache affect latency? Our users need real-time replies sometimes.
[04:42] Leo: Good point — the Console's suggestions include tradeoff curves. For that route we set a small batching window and conservative caching so p95 only increased by 10ms but cost dropped substantially. You can pick points on the curve: max-cost-saver, balanced, low-latency.
[04:58] Samir: Security: what audit logs do you retain and can we ship them to our SIEM?
[05:04] Maya: Yes, full audit logging is available; you can export to S3 or send to syslog/CloudWatch, and we have an integration to forward to common SIEMs. For Private we can keep logs on-prem.
[05:14] Samir: KMS support? We need BYOK and HSM references.
[05:18] Leo: We integrate with customer KMS providers and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. We'll share the spec.
[05:25] Tom: Networking — we have strict egress rules, can Redwood run inside our VPC?
[05:31] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private can run in your V P C or on-prem package. For the hosted route we offer peered connections and VPC egress restrictions. We'll include a network runbook for your team.
[05:41] Aisha: On the model side, can we pin model versions for reproducibility?
[05:46] Leo: Yep, pin model version and rollout policies. Console shows version lineage and rollout metrics so you can see if a new version increases token usage or latency.
[05:56] Priya: When you show cost breakdown, can we tie it to our internal chargeback codes?
[06:00] Leo: Absolutely — tags can map to your chargeback codes and we can export allocation CSVs for FinOps ingestion.
[06:08] Priya: Nice. That will save us time.
[06:10] Maya: Quick demo of the per-route cost explorer — filtering by team, product, model family and then exporting a weekly report.
[06:20] [screen change]
[06:23] Leo: Here's the cost waterfall: model compute, memory overhead, network egress, and a line for caching savings. You can click into a route and see sample traces to diagnose token spikes.
[06:36] Tom: Sample traces — is that raw prompt content? We have PII concerns.
[06:40] Leo: Good callout. Traces by default are redacted; you can opt into full traces but that requires specific policies and retention settings. For the pilot we'll keep redacted traces.
[06:52] Aisha: Can we run a benchmark comparing OpenAI vs Redwood hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:56] Maya: Yes that's the pilot we usually run. Leo will outline the benchmark plan: model parity tests, latency SLOs, token-cost per attempt, and an A/B for quality.
[07:09] Leo: Plan would be 48-72 hour runs per model scenario, controlled traffic replay, and we'll measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, and per-token cost. We can run the same prompts you run against OpenAI to compare.
[07:23] Priya: For billback, we need a predicted monthly spend after optimizations. Do you produce that?
[07:29] Leo: The Console's Forecast view will show baseline and post-Optimize forecast; we include conservative and optimistic bands.
[07:36] Samir: Do you offer SOC2?
[07:39] Maya: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO bytes and our compliance pack. Also we support SAML SSO and RBAC per org.
[07:49] Aisha: One more — do you have developer SDKs so we can add headers for route mapping?
[07:54] Leo: Yes, SDKs for Java, Python, Node — header examples are in the docs. Many customers instrument at the edge to capture product context.
[08:04] Tom: Okay what's the timeline to get a pilot running if we want Dedicated?
[08:08] Maya: For Dedicated it's typically 2-6 weeks depending on provisioning and approvals; hosted pilot can be immediate — we can spin up routes in days. Private on-prem takes longer.
[08:20] Priya: Cost — do you offer trial credits or discounted pilot pricing?
[08:24] Maya: We do pilot credits and reduced pilot rates; we'll include pilot SOW in the email.
[08:30] Aisha: Great. Can you show the anomaly detection for route-level tickets?
[08:33] Leo: Sure — here's anomaly timeline, auto-detection of token drifts, and auto-created incident with a link to traces and recommended rollback.
[08:46] Tom: That would help our ops team.
[08:48] Maya: At this point we had a couple customer questions about vendor lock and migration plan.
[08:53] Aisha: Yes, if we start on hosted how painful to migrate to Dedicated or Private later?
[08:58] Leo: Migration path is supported — same API surface, exportable configs, and model artifacts. We're mindful about not locking you in; we provide tooling for replays and config diffs.
[09:10] Priya: Any gotchas on quantization quality regressions?
[09:14] Leo: Quant profiles are recommended per-model and we tie that into evals — you can run a small eval set and we'll show quality regression risk. It's part of Optimize.
[09:24] Samir: Last sec: can Redwood provide an architecture diagram showing data flows for hosted vs private?
[09:29] Maya: Yes we'll attach that to the follow-up.
[09:32] Aisha: Okay I think that's the main list. Next steps?
[09:35] Maya: Recap: we'll send pilot SOW and pricing by Friday (2027-11-12), Leo will send benchmark plan, and Riverstone to share network egress constraints and sample workloads. We'll tentatively schedule the benchmark week of 11/22.
[09:49] Priya: Sounds good.
[09:50] Tom: Thanks team.
[09:52] Maya: One more note — competitors? We know you use OpenAI, any others in eval?
[09:58] Aisha: Mostly OpenAI and a little Anthropic. We're curious about cost differences.
[10:03] Leo: Great. Any final questions?
[10:06] [brief silence]
[10:10] Maya: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with the docs.
[10:13] Aisha: Thanks!
[10:15] Tom: Thanks all.
[10:17] [call ends]
notes: Realistic transcript with occasional mis-hears (e.g., V P C spelled out) and natural speech. References to shared artifacts: pilot SOW (link to be provided), SOC2 + network runbook to be attached in follow-up email.
